title: Fractional CMO-in-a-box via Claude Skills pack
one_liner: Productize a Claude Skills bundle (brand voice, content atomizer, DR copy, email sequences, keyword research, lead magnets, newsletter, positioning, orchestrator) and sell it as a fractional CMO install for boring brands.
evidence_quote: Full walkthrough: Brand Voice, Content Atomizer, Direct Response Copy (my favorite), Email Sequences, Keyword Research, Lead Magnets, Newsletter, Positioning Angles, and the Orchestrator — a fractional CMO in a box. Plus: AI Creative Strategist for image/video prompts.
why_it_works: Packages years of marketing judgment into reusable Skills so delivery is install + configure, not custom strategy every week. Distinct from newsletter-atomizer desk (single workflow) — this is a full CMO stack sold as a product.
notes: oEmbed-verified The Boring Marketer. Public skill store link in description; harvest idea only — no revenue claims.

title: Skills + Claude Code SEO/site build for one boring local partner
one_liner: Use revenue-oriented Claude Skills + Claude Code to research keywords and ship a site for one boring local business you partner with (or own a slice of), then run demand — not content-only Skills.
evidence_quote: Entire marketing done in 2 days. Local boring business I'm a partner in: found keywords, built website in Claude Code. Now $30-40K/month. The leverage is real.
why_it_works: Pairs AI build speed with a real local demand partner so the Skill output is measured in jobs/calls. Thin vs generic Main Street AI firm — one partner, Skills-first build.
notes: Companion short blwSIdeQixk same thesis. Anecdote is creator's; not a guarantee.

title: Front-end-only demand desk for a boring trade (never touch the wrench)
one_liner: Pick a boring Maps-dense trade (pool, HVAC-adjacent), find an operator strong at the work and weak at marketing, own only SEO/ads/automation front-end, and feed them booked jobs — never buy a truck or learn the trade.
evidence_quote: the best AI business i've seen this year doesn't touch the AI industry. it's pointing AI marketing skills at a boring local trade… open google maps… pick a trade you have zero interest in… find the operator who's great at the work and bad at marketing. you bring the customers, they do the job. you never touch a wrench… own the front end only: seo, ads, automation.
why_it_works: Separates demand ownership from fulfillment capacity; operator supplies trucks/insurance while you own the funnel. Distinct from front-end marketing partnership already logged — this is explicit no-ops / Maps-first JV framing from the Main Street AI video + public X thesis.
notes: Evidence also mirrored on public X/@boringmarketer via twiiit harvest. Deduped vs front-end-local-trade-marketing-026 (kept as Maps+never-wrench SOP).

title: Apify Maps → AI leak-score → Zapier custom-pitch machine
one_liner: Scrape Google Maps with Apify, have AI flag site leaks (no email capture / no click-to-call / no offer), auto-build named-owner pitch assets in Zapier, then run hyperlocal Meta — sell the machine as a done-for-you desk.
evidence_quote: The machine, built in Zapier: scrape Google Maps with Apify, read each site and let AI flag the leak (no email capture, no click-to-call, no offer), then auto-build a custom pitch with the owner's name on it. Real example inside: 20 Atlanta HVAC companies, all with the same 3 leaks.
why_it_works: Turns prospecting into a repeatable Zapier workflow with free skill to regenerate Zaps. Thin vs maps-gap-score-047 — this cites the full Apify+Zapier+Meta machine with HVAC leak pattern.
notes: Chapters explicitly cover Apify+Maps, scoring, pitch asset, hyperlocal FB. Free skill mentioned in description.

title: Sell revenue Skills (keyword→site) instead of content Skills
one_liner: Position and sell Claude Skills that go 0→1 on a local boring business (keywords → Claude Code site → demand) rather than Skills that only generate social posts.
evidence_quote: Most AI skills generate content. This one has generated real revenue. … Go from 0 to 1. Used this for a local boring business, found keywords, built website in Claude Code.
why_it_works: Buyers pay for outcomes tied to revenue workflows; content Skills are commoditized. Product packaging play distinct from running the local partner yourself.
notes: Short; pairs with Rv2DasDaB8g. No income guarantees.

title: Free restaurant sandwich boards with sold bottom ad slots
one_liner: Give restaurants a free dry-erase A-frame for specials; sell 6 local ad slots on the bottom (~$600/yr each); collect before printing; upsell GBP/reputation/websites after delivery photo.
evidence_quote: She gives restaurants a nice board for free, then sells advertising space on the bottom of it to other local businesses. One board placed brings in around $3,000 a year… Sell each of the six spots for $600 a year, collected upfront… you do not print anything until you have sold the ad spots.
why_it_works: Host gets free utility; advertisers get captive wait-line attention; cash collected before print kills inventory risk. Upsell path to digital retainers.
notes: Rachel interview; also Apple Ep #327 framing. Public newsletter cite. No income guarantees.

title: Vacant-land contract assignment to spec builders (builder-first)
one_liner: Get builders' lot buy-box first from new-construction Zillow listings, put vacant parcels under assignable contract below that number, assign to the builder, never own the land.
evidence_quote: how they built a land flipping business by helping home builders find off-market lots… get a builder's buy box first, then go find landowners willing to sell for less, keeping the difference as profit without usually buying the land themselves.
why_it_works: Demand is pre-qualified; capital risk stays low with assignable contracts + feasibility outs. Thin in corpus vs house wholesaling.
notes: Also newsletter profitable-side-hustle-to-start-with-no-money. Requires RE attorney review of assignable contracts — Brandon legal gate.

title: Shared EDDM home-services postcard co-op
one_liner: Design one thick shared postcard, sell exclusive category slots to local home-service pros via FB business groups, print after sold, mail via USPS EDDM to income-filtered single-family routes.
evidence_quote: Josh turned $90 into $50K in a year selling ad space on postcards that get mailed to thousands of homes. He finds local businesses in Facebook groups, closes 95% of his deals over text… connects local businesses to local homeowners through the mail.
why_it_works: EDDM needs no mailing list; exclusive categories create urgency; unit economics clear before print. Distinct from sandwich-board (mail vs foot traffic).

title: Nitro cold-brew iced-coffee event cart
one_liner: Build a Husky tool-cart with bag-in-box cold brew + nitrogen tap; sell iced coffee at car shows/festivals/car washes with big ICED COFFEE signage; 30-second pours, no espresso machine.
evidence_quote: It's iced coffee… selling it from a gutted Home Depot tool cart with a nitro tap system bolted inside… Cup cost: roughly $3… Selling price: $8 to $8.50… Just tap, pour, cap, hand it over. Thirty seconds per cup.
why_it_works: Speed + obvious signage + event density beats cafe overhead; low skill pour. Permits/health gates required.
notes: Marc interview via newsletter; Apple Ep #297 referenced. No income guarantees.

title: Dirty-soda / specialty lemonade event cart
one_liner: Same low-overhead cart model as nitro coffee but with fruit syrups + sparkling water (or specialty lemonades) for events — sub-$1.50 COGS targets and under-$1.5k startup framing.
evidence_quote: Dirty sodas/ specialty lemonades. Fruit syrups run about $10 to $15 per bottle and yield 30 to 40 servings. Add sparkling water, ice, and a cup and your cost per drink lands around $1.50. Sell them for $6 to $8… Startup is under $1,500 total.
why_it_works: Trend drink with cafe-like margins without lease; same event GTM as coffee cart. Distinct SKU/lane from nitro coffee.
notes: Adjacent cart concepts listed in same NL (cotton candy, nitro matcha). Harvest one clear SKU.

title: Agricultural drone crop-spraying service
one_liner: Run automated spray drones as 'air traffic control' for local farms: mission on phone, swap batteries/tanks, chase seasonal demand north→south; validate demand with Keyword Planner first.
evidence_quote: The business is agricultural drone spraying… fully automated so you set a mission on your phone, hit go, and the drone takes off… sprays the field, and comes back when the battery is low or the tank is empty… Mike described it as being air traffic control.
why_it_works: Labor shortage + precision spraying demand; seasonal travel extends utilization. Heavy regulatory/FAA and chemical licensing gates.
notes: Thin category in corpus. Licensing/FAA Part 137-equivalent compliance is Brandon legal/physical gate.

title: Whatnot / TikTok Live auction resale shows
one_liner: Source a tight category (e.g. soccer jerseys), go live on Whatnot (high intent) or TikTok Live auctions, sell with emotion after buying with math; optimize for show density not follower count.
evidence_quote: Kip went live two days before our interview- selling soccer jerseys, a category with zero competition on the platform. He sold 90 jerseys in two hours… Whatnot is community-driven with high buyer intent… TikTok just launched live auctions.
why_it_works: Live scarcity + niche category emptiness; Whatnot intent > vanity followers. Ops-heavy sourcing/fulfillment.
notes: Public NL; no income guarantees. Platform ToS/compliance gates.

title: Claude Skills / tiny-tool digital product packs
one_liner: Package workflows you already use into Claude Skills (or tiny tools), price single skills ~$19–$29 or bundles ~$49–$99, sell via a simple sales page with delivery + upsells.
evidence_quote: Ryan prices his full stack of 25 skills at $99. If you're starting from scratch, price a single skill between $19 and $29 and a bundle of three to five somewhere around $49 to $79. The goal in week one isn't volume. It's a paying customer who validates that the product works.
why_it_works: One build, many sales; week-one validation focus beats perfection. Distinct from BM fractional-CMO box (agency install) — this is DTC digital product.
notes: Chris NL featuring Ryan's Skills packs.

title: Scratch-your-itch agent-built micro-SaaS (then sell it)
one_liner: Have an agentic coder (e.g. Grok bot + Replit) build a tool for your own daily pain (inbox locker example), wire Stripe during the build, use it yourself, then sell the same micro-product to others with the same pain.
evidence_quote: about thirty minutes later I had a working software product… locks Gmail and my Mail app outside of one set window every morning… Grok bot even wired up Stripe during the build… Build these for other people. If you can do this in half an hour, you can do it for a business owner who cannot.
why_it_works: Dogfooding proves willingness-to-pay; agent collapses build/test loop. Also YT gmwDBNcFXFU companion.
notes: oEmbed-related YT Make Money With This New AI Agent. No income guarantees.

title: Productized $1k AI opportunity assessment for SMBs
one_liner: 45-min Zoom discovery → Claude-generated tool/recommendation report delivered for ~$1,000; upsell process optimization, Zapier builds, custom GPTs, and speed-to-lead agents.
evidence_quote: He charges $1,000 to do a 45-minute Zoom call with a small business owner, writes up a report of how different ready-made tools to help them… Corey sits down… runs the transcript through Claude, gets a list of tools… and delivers a polished report.
why_it_works: Paid diagnostic filters tire-kickers and creates natural implementation upsells. Distinct from full SMB AI retainers already in corpus — this is the wedge product.
notes: Corey playbook via Chris NL / Ep #292. Free local AI meetup GTM mentioned.

title: OpenClaw / personal AI OS install + executive retainer
one_liner: Install a personal AI control plane connected to email/docs/history for executives, train the team, then retain monthly to keep memory/files/tools updated — setup workshops framed at a few thousand dollars.
evidence_quote: A basic setup and training session for an executive team runs $2,000 to $5,000. You connect it to their email and calendar, fill out their profile and memory files… Corporations will also pay for ongoing access… a monthly retainer… Go set up OpenClaw… and charge companies to do the same for them.
why_it_works: Companies lack personal AI ops; install+train is a clear deliverable, retainer compounds as memory grows. Also YT vQ3SxSy8J0g / Ep #278.
notes: Security/privacy review is a hard gate before any client data connect.

title: Build-in-public AI agent journey + $10 pre-order validation
one_liner: Give an agentic system a money goal, film/post the experiments (wins and fails), and validate demand with paid $10 pre-orders before building the product the audience reacts to.
evidence_quote: Give it a goal, not a plan… Post what it's doing. Film yourself talking to it… Test demand: If your posts get traction, put up a pre-order page and charge $10 to hold a spot… Robbie had $6,000 in hand before he built a single thing.
why_it_works: Audience filters which agent experiments become products; paid pre-orders beat vanity waitlists. YT l0Vqm0ZIySc companion.
notes: Platform/tool names evolve; harvest the GTM pattern not a specific vendor lock-in.

title: Productized design subscription (DesignJoy-style queue)
one_liner: Sell unlimited design as a flat monthly subscription with one-request-in-queue rules, next-day/fast TTV, no calls/contracts; launch via Product Hunt/forums even without an audience.
evidence_quote: Brett's idea was a productized design agency… you just go to his website, pick a plan, pay, and get designs back the next day or two. No contracts, calls required… He calls it lowering the TTV… His website DesignJoy a subscription model.
why_it_works: Speed + packaging removes agency sales friction; subscription stabilizes cashflow. Distinct from pass4 AI design studio (AI-production focus) — this is the classic productized human/taste queue SOP.
notes: Also lists productized copy, short-form editing, thumbnails, podcast editing as sibling formats.

title: AI-era human editorial / brand journalism retainers
one_liner: Sell experience-led articles and editing to brands that still pay premium for human voice ($1k-class posts), using AI as research/draft assist without replacing judgment — portfolio via Upwork + cold outreach.
evidence_quote: I sat down with Steph Spector, a freelance writer, editor, and coach… why companies still pay her up to $1,200 per article, how she uses tools like Claude, Gemini, and ChatGPT without letting them replace her voice… why real human experience is becoming more valuable.
why_it_works: Commodity AI copy floods the market; lived-experience editorial becomes the scarce input. Distinct from generic tech writing already logged — premium brand journalism positioning.
notes: oEmbed-verified Ep #333. Deduped vs human-led freelance tech writing.
